worker_target_description: Vaidis et al. (2024), induced-compliance replication of Croyle and Cooper Experiment 1. The broad description and p. 15 locator identify multiple primary Welch tests: postessay attitude and attitude change, each comparing high-choice counterattitudinal essay (HC-CE) against low-choice counterattitudinal essay (LC-CE) or high-choice neutral essay (HC-NE). A unique test is not specified.
worker_notes: Identity assessment: canonical text begins with the title A Multilab Replication of the Induced-Compliance Paradigm of Cognitive Dissonance, authors David C. Vaidis, Willem W. A. Sleegers and colleagues, DOI 10.1177/25152459231213375, and Registered Replication Report designation, matching the supplied replication reference. Text includes the full 26-page article, methods, results, discussion, and references; it is a primary replication report rather than an abstract or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Only n_r and reported_success are assigned; other fields are placeholders. The row description Induced compliance. and p.15 locator do not uniquely identify one of the four primary tests, so n_r remains null and target_match remains null. Candidate final-group sums from Table 4, p.15: postessay HC-CE vs LC-CE: 1,448 + 1,343 = 2,791 participants (same-test printed d = −0.03, p = .79); postessay HC-CE vs HC-NE: 1,448 + 1,031 = 2,479 participants (d = 0.26, p < .001); attitude change HC-CE vs LC-CE: 1,060 + 937 = 1,997 participants (d = 0.017, p = .35); attitude change HC-CE vs HC-NE: 1,060 + 726 = 1,786 participants (d = 0.31, p < .001). These are sums of mutually exclusive randomized conditions for each outcome, not sums across outcomes. No candidate is selected. Page 13 also reports aggregate primary sample totals 3,822 for postessay attitude and 2,724 for attitude change; these are not uniquely target-test Ns. Reported_success is the authors' explicit narrative verdict on replication of the classic dissonance effect; their discussion also acknowledges positive counterattitudinal-versus-neutral differences, so failed does not mean all comparisons were nonsignificant.
